quote: I really wouldn't recommend solar panels for your home
stewart_read: Rep disqualifies the home based purely on a satellite image glance seconds into the roof question, without asking about roof age/type or exploring actual sun exposure per side of the house.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep is trying to set realistic expectations early to avoid wasting time on an unsellable lead.
coaching_implication: Roof/shading DQ should follow the full verify roof question, not replace it — 'off the rip' judgment from satellite imagery isn't a substitute for the qualifying conversation.

quote: Well, I have, sun all morning on the front of my house and all afternoon on the back.
stewart_read: Customer directly rebuts the DQ with a specific, credible claim about sun exposure; rep does not investigate or flip this into a reason to proceed, she reaffirms the DQ instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep lacks a process for handling a customer disputing a satellite-based DQ, so she defaults to restating the tree concern.
coaching_implication: When a customer challenges a satellite DQ with specifics, the move is to note it and offer an on-site/design-team review rather than re-asserting the same read.

quote: I'm gonna ask someone else their opinion,
stewart_read: Rep places a roughly one-minute hold to consult a supervisor on a borderline shading call — a scenario outside her ability to resolve alone.
coaching_implication: Fine as a mechanism, but the supervisor consult should produce an actual next step (site assessment offer) rather than just reaffirming the DQ verbally.

quote: somebody who's willing to actually look at what's on
stewart_read: Second touch of the same sun-exposure pushback; rep responds with a technical explanation of panel placement rather than addressing her request for an actual look at her property.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be trying to educate her on why it wouldn't work rather than string her along — but this forgoes the appointment entirely without ever verifying the claim.
coaching_implication: This is the second time the same objection landed unaddressed — coach the rep to acknowledge it explicitly and offer to route to a specialist for a real look rather than repeating the tree lecture.

quote: I just keep hoping that somebody will look at what sun I get and not look at threes.
stewart_read: Third and final touch of the same unresolved concern, delivered right as the rep closes the call — never acknowledged or resolved.
coaching_implication: By the third repetition of the same specific, reasonable pushback, ending the call with 'wish you the best of luck' abandons a lead who was still actively arguing to stay qualified.

quote: Yeah. Anyway, thank you. Yeah. No problem. Wish you the best of luck in, you know, everything. Okay?
stewart_read: Call ends abruptly with no next step, no offer of a specialist follow-up, and no acknowledgment of the customer's repeated, unresolved objection.
coaching_implication: Even a hard-looking DQ should end with an owned next step (e.g., 'I'll have our design team take a real look and follow up') rather than a flat goodbye.
